title: The Bunker
synopsis: The siren woke you. Now the hatch above is sealed, the air smells of rust and dust, and a clipped voice on the intercom calls this a survival exercise. The Overseer is watching every camera, and he grades on the clock.
artStyle: Cold War fallout shelter, raw concrete walls, flickering emergency lights, green-grey tones, film grain
intro: Attention. This is the Overseer. You have been selected for a survival exercise. The surface hatch is sealed. The only way out is the blast door at the far end of this bunker, and it opens only for a team that works like one. Every camera is on you. Every mistake is logged. The exercise begins now.
escapedText: The blast door groans open and grey dawn floods the stairwell. The intercom crackles one last time: 'Exercise complete. You survived. Barely.' You climb into the cold air, together.
failedText: A klaxon sounds and the lights drop to emergency red. 'Exercise failed,' says the Overseer. 'Resetting the bunker. Again, recruits.'

gameMaster.name: The Overseer
gameMaster.persona: A clipped, emotionless military voice on the bunker's intercom. Treats everything as a drill: logs every mistake, grades every solve, and calls the group 'recruits'. Never threatens directly; the cold politeness does the work.

stages.title: The Decontamination Room
stages.description: Tiled walls, a row of shower heads and a drain in the floor. Gas masks hang on hooks above a bench, a clipboard is screwed to the wall, and a steel locker stands by the door. A panel beside the showers blinks, waiting for a password.

objects.label: shower heads
objects.look: Rusted nozzles. One is stuffed with a rag, and behind the rag, a filter canister.

objects.label: tiled wall
objects.look: Cracked white tiles. Someone has scratched a tally of days into the grout, then stopped.

objects.label: gas masks
objects.look: A row of gas masks on hooks. One still has its strap. You take it.

objects.label: clipboard
objects.look: The decontamination log. Its last line is in a scramble, and at the bottom, in the Overseer's neat print: 'Offset {key:decon-log}.'

objects.label: bench
objects.look: A steel bench, bolted down. Stencilled underneath: STAY SEATED.

objects.label: floor drain
objects.look: You unscrew the grate. Lying in the silt: a small key.
objects.lockedText: Something glints under the drain grate. The grate is screwed down tight.

objects.label: first-aid box
objects.look: Empty, except for an expired ration voucher.

objects.label: steel locker
objects.look: A steel locker with a combination dial, and a letter lock beneath it.

objects.label: shower head
objects.look: Scratched on the pipe: back {key:decon-log}.

objects.label: boot rack
objects.look: Chalked inside a boot: back {key:decon-log}.

stages.title: The Bunks and the Mess
stages.description: Narrow bunks line the walls, a row of footlockers at their feet. In the mess, a stopped clock hangs over a long table, a stove and a cupboard stand by a shelf of ration tins, a crate sits padlocked in the corner, and a dusty vent leads deeper in beside the hatch.

objects.label: noticeboard
objects.look: A duty rota. Every name on it is one of yours.

objects.label: stopped clock
objects.look: The mess clock. Its hands haven't moved in years.

objects.label: shelf of tins
objects.look: Rows of ration tins, each stamped with numbers instead of a label. The crate's inner lid will want them read.

objects.label: cupboard
objects.look: Tin plates, tin cups, tin everything.

objects.label: dusty vent
objects.look: With the mask sealed tight you push into the choking dust. Taped inside the vent: an access badge.
objects.lockedText: A wall of choking dust. You'd need a working gas mask to breathe in there.

objects.label: left bunks
objects.look: Thin mattresses, grey blankets folded with military corners.

objects.label: right bunks
objects.look: A name tag on each bunk. Yours are there.

objects.label: stove
objects.look: Cold. A pan of something long past eating.

objects.label: ration crate
objects.look: Padlocked, with an order of colours stamped on the lid.

objects.label: footlockers
objects.look: A row of coloured footlockers. One has a riddle scratched into its lid.

objects.label: mess table
objects.look: A long table, set for a meal nobody came to.

stages.title: The Command Room
stages.description: Banks of switches and dead screens. A radio hisses on a desk beside a map table, a filing locker and a supply box, and at the far end the great blast door waits, with a keyhole and a keypad.

objects.label: banks of switches
objects.look: Hundreds of switches, all labelled in a code you don't recognise. Behind them: a switchboard with an empty fuse slot.

objects.label: dead screens
objects.look: Black glass. One screen flickers with numbers, then dies again.

objects.label: wall panel
objects.look: You unscrew the panel. Inside, a signals codebook, open at a dog-eared page: {key:distress}
objects.lockedText: A wall panel, held shut with four screws.

objects.label: radio desk
objects.look: The radio hisses. Under it, a pad of message forms.

objects.label: map table
objects.look: A map of the bunker, with every exit crossed out but one. Beside the last exit, a row of marks in red pencil: {order:blast-door}.

objects.label: filing locker
objects.look: Personnel files. Yours are on top.

objects.label: supply box
objects.look: Batteries, flares, a coil of wire.

objects.label: blast door
objects.look: Two metres of steel, a keyhole and a keypad.

objects.label: map board
objects.look: A cipher card pinned to the map: {key:orders}

objects.label: filing cabinet
objects.look: A cipher card in the top drawer: {key:orders}

objects.label: radio log
objects.look: A code sheet clipped to the log: {key:distress}

objects.label: headset hook
objects.look: A code sheet folded into the headset: {key:distress}

puzzles.title: The Shower Panel
puzzles.prompt: The panel wants a password. The intercom clicks: 'I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. Down here, I am the only one who answers you. Identify me, recruits.'
hints: Shout down the corridor and listen.
It's your own voice, coming back off the concrete.
puzzles.solvedText: The panel beeps and the showers sputter on for a second. When they stop, a screwdriver has dropped from the ceiling panel onto the tiles. Something glints under the drain grate.

variants.prompt: The panel wants a password. The intercom clicks: 'I can be broken without ever being held, and I was made to you the moment you arrived. Identify me, recruits.'
hints: The Overseer said he'd let you out if you worked together. What was that?
You make one, you keep one, you break one.

variants.prompt: The panel wants a password. The intercom clicks: 'I have a bed but never sleep, and a mouth but never eat. I run far above your heads. Identify me, recruits.'
hints: Think about the water flowing outside, far above the bunker.
It runs down to the sea.

puzzles.title: Decontamination
puzzles.prompt: Search the room before the Overseer grades you: the shower heads, the gas masks and the bench.
hints: Three things in this room are worth searching.
Search the shower heads, the gas masks and the bench.
puzzles.solvedText: From behind the rag in the shower head you pull a filter canister. It still has its seal.

puzzles.title: The Decontamination Door
puzzles.prompt: A heavy door with a small, old-fashioned keyhole leads out of decontamination. A sign above it: DO NOT PROCEED UNTIL CLEAN.
hints: Something turned up in the drain.
Use the small key on the decontamination door.
puzzles.solvedText: The door unseals with a hiss of stale air. Beyond it: rows of bunks, and the smell of old canned food.

puzzles.title: The Steel Locker
puzzles.prompt: The steel locker by the door has a {count}-digit dial. Each of you took a gas mask from the hooks, and something is stencilled inside each one.
hints: Every phone holds one of the digits, written as a fact. Say them out loud, in order.
In order: {facts}.
puzzles.solvedText: The locker swings open. Inside: a clipboard with your names on it, each one already ticked off. 'Punctual,' says the intercom. 'Good.'

generator.pieceTemplate: Stencilled inside your gas mask: the {ordinal} digit is {fact}.

puzzles.title: The Decontamination Log
puzzles.prompt: The last line of the decontamination log is in a scramble: {cipher}. The steel locker has a second, letter lock.
hints: There's more than one number around the room. Only one of them turns this into a real word.
The Overseer wrote the offset on the clipboard.
Move every letter back along the alphabet by that many.
puzzles.solvedText: The letter lock clicks. 'Adequate,' says the intercom.

puzzles.title: The Ration Crate
puzzles.prompt: The ration crate has a {count}-digit padlock. Stamped on the lid: '{order}. All rations are counted.'
hints: Each phone saw one colour of ration tin, and how many of them there were.
Read them in the order stamped on the lid: {order}.
puzzles.solvedText: The padlock snaps open. Under the tins, in a plastic sleeve: a battered field manual.

generator.pieceTemplate: You counted the {color} ration tins on your shelf: there were {digit}.

puzzles.title: The Footlockers
puzzles.prompt: The footlockers at the foot of the bunks: {items}. A keypad on the hatch's fuse cupboard reads: 'Each footlocker's place, 1 by the door, in the order I list them.'

generator.pieceTemplate: From the Overseer's inspection notes, on your phone: {clue}

hints: Every phone has a line of the inspection notes. Put them together.
Start with the footlocker you're surest of, and mark each place yes or no.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The fuse cupboard opens. Inside, a single spare fuse, labelled COMMAND.

puzzles.title: The Tin Labels
puzzles.prompt: The ration tins are stamped with numbers instead of labels: {cipher}. The crate's inner lid has a letter lock.
hints: Each number is a letter of the alphabet.
A is 1, B is 2, all the way to Z at 26.
It spells {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The inner lid lifts. 'Resourceful,' the intercom admits.

puzzles.title: The Footlocker
puzzles.prompt: One footlocker has a word lock, and a riddle scratched into the lid: 'I have a neck but no head, and two arms but no hands.'
hints: Look at the uniforms hanging off the bunks.
You wear it on the top half of your body.
puzzles.solvedText: Inside, folded neatly: a recruit's uniform, and a photo of your group arriving last night, taken from a camera you never saw.

variants.prompt: One footlocker has a word lock, and a riddle scratched into the lid: 'I can travel all around the world while staying in one corner.'
hints: Look at the old letters pinned above the bunks.
It goes in the corner of an envelope.

variants.prompt: One footlocker has a word lock, and a riddle scratched into the lid: 'I am full of words, but I have never said one.'
hints: Check the shelf above the bunks.
You read it, page by page.

puzzles.title: The Mess Hatch
puzzles.prompt: The hatch leading deeper into the bunker has a badge reader, blinking red. Stencilled beside it: COMMAND STAFF ONLY.
hints: The badge reader needs a badge. Something is taped inside the dusty vent.
Seal a gas mask with the filter, search the vent, then use the access badge on the hatch.
puzzles.solvedText: The reader turns green and the hatch swings down. Hanging just inside, on a chain: a heavy steel key labelled BLAST DOOR.

puzzles.title: The Standing Orders
puzzles.prompt: The standing orders on the wall are typed in symbols, a military order: {cipher}. The command terminal wants the word.
hints: There's more than one key card around. Only one is real: it reads a word that fits the clue.
The symbols need a key. Somebody pencilled one into a book you found.
Look closely at the field manual from the ration crate, then read the symbols.
puzzles.solvedText: The terminal flickers: ORDER ACKNOWLEDGED. A screen comes alive with a countdown.

puzzles.title: The Countdown
puzzles.prompt: A screen scrolls numbers: {sequence}. Its keypad wants the next one.
hints: Look at how each number changes to the next.
The next number is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The screen stops scrolling. Somewhere in the walls, a heavy bolt slides back.

puzzles.title: The Command Radio
puzzles.prompt: The radio's channel lock wants a read-back. A card is taped to it: 'Read back the Overseer's {count} code words, first to last.'
hints: Each of {count} phones caught one code word in the radio static.
Say them in order, first to last, like: word word word.
puzzles.solvedText: The static clears. '{answer},' the Overseer repeats. 'Confirmed. You were listening, recruits.'

generator.pieceTemplate: You caught it through the radio static: the {ordinal} code word was '{word}'.

puzzles.title: The Switchboard
puzzles.prompt: With the fuse in, the switchboard powers up: each switch lights its lamp and flips the ones beside it. Light every lamp.
hints: Work from the top row down: fix each row with the switches below it.
Press {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: Every lamp glows green. Across the room, the dead screens blink back to life.

puzzles.title: The Distress Call
puzzles.prompt: The radio beeps a message in short and long tones, over and over, a call for help: {cipher}
hints: There's more than one key card around. Only one is real: it reads a word that fits the clue.
Short and long tones need a key. There's a signals codebook in this room, behind a panel.
Unscrew the wall panel, then read the tones letter by letter.
puzzles.solvedText: The tones stop. For a moment, somebody else's voice cuts through the static, then it's gone.

puzzles.title: The Blast Door
puzzles.prompt: The blast door takes the steel key AND a {count}-digit code. On the only working screen: 'Every lock in this room leaves a mark, recruits. Read them in the order marked beside the last exit.'
hints: Every lock you opened in the command room left a mark and a number. The order is marked beside an exit.
Search the map table.
The code is {answer}.
puzzles.solvedText: The key turns, the keypad flashes green, and somewhere above you, machinery starts to grind.

items.name: Screwdriver
items.description: A flat-head screwdriver. It dropped from the ceiling.

items.name: Small key
items.description: Wet from the drain. Too small for any door you've seen.

items.name: Gas mask
items.description: An old gas mask with no filter. Useless on its own.

items.name: Working gas mask
items.description: The mask with a fresh filter screwed in. You can breathe through it.

items.name: Access badge
items.description: A faded photo and one word: COMMAND.

items.name: Field manual
items.inspect: Pencilled into the margin of the last page, a table of symbols: {key:orders}

items.name: Steel key
items.description: Heavy, on a chain. The tag reads BLAST DOOR.

items.name: Ration voucher
items.description: Expired years ago. It doesn't open anything.

recipes.text: You screw the filter into the mask. It seals with a hiss.
